newsitem.title: USA: Universal withdraws Perry offer, sees loss.
newsitem.headline: Universal withdraws Perry offer, sees loss.

text.p: Universal International Inc said Tuesday it has withdrawn its offer to purchase the leases and inventory of about 90 stores and the warehouse of Perry Brothers Inc in Lufkin, Texas.

"We've decied to withdraw from that with Perry. The timing of having to raise the equity needed for the acquisition overlapping with the negotiations we were in because of the problems we had with our last bank, and the contraction of our business from wholesale and retail to a retail business, became a little too much for the investment community to swallow," said Mark Ravich, Universal chief executive.
"We've released them a little bit early from their obligation to us to wait before re-evaluating their options," he told the company's annual meeting here.
When Universal announced the proposed deal in early April, it had said it planned to convert Perry's stores from variety stores into closeout stores similar to Universal's Only Deals chain.
In another development, Ravich said Universal expects to report a small loss in the 1997 third quarter, be profitable in the fourth quarter and incur a loss for the 1997 year.
"We'll have a significant loss for the year with our winding down wholesale," Ravich told Reuters.
"To us this is really a restructuring transition year," he said after the annual meeting.
Universal reported a 1996 loss equal of $4.3 million or a loss of $0.88 a share.
